about.0:
Georges Bataille (...) imagined the existence in the human being of an eye specific
to contemplate the sun: the pineal eye, a gland
situated beneath the cranial vault that, unlike the eyes caught in the horizontality of everyday becoming, of what offers
itself to the gaze, allows us to raise ourselves and see the sun face
to face, like the eagle of the ancients. The pineal eye is, for Bataille, the
confirmation of the human being’s yearning to raise himself above his
earthly condition. This uncontained desire to see the sun face
to face would mark, according to the author, the evolution of
man from his inclined, quadruped position,
bound to the ground with a horizontal gaze, to the upright
urge to contemplate the sun directly, which
would definitively distance him from his first origin as an animal. Thus, drunk with sun, he can
surrender himself completely to the anguish and the nausea
that limitless space, absolute emptiness produces. The pineal
eye, an organ that allows man to identify himself directly with what
he contemplates, converts him into sun, that is,
becomes, paradoxically, a blind sun or a blinding
sun.
(...) Bataille, who found parodic correspondences between all things in the universe, saw this
pineal eye in close relation to the anus. “The Solar Anus” is precisely the title of a 1927 text.
Mercedez Replinger/Marisa Flórido César
